title: The fathers named in prayers and spells
source_text: Ἑξῆς δὲ τούτοις ὁ Κέλσος ἐπιτρέχων τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς πρώτης βίβλου Μωϋσέως. ἥτις ἐπιγέγραπται Γένεσις, φησὶν ὡς ἄρα ἐπεχείρησαν γενεαλογεῖν αὑτοὺς ἀπὸ πρώτης σπορᾶς γοήτων καὶ πλάνων ἀνθρώπων, ἀμυδρὰς καὶ ἀμφιβόλους φωνὰς ἐν σκότῳ που κρυφίους ἐπιμαρτυρόμενοι καὶ τοῖς ἀμαθέσι καὶ ἀνοήτοις παρεξηγούμενοι, καὶ ταῦτα μηδὲ πώποτ᾿ ἐν πολλῷ τῷ πρόσθεν χρόνῳ τοῦ τοιοῦδε μηδ᾿ ἀμφισβητηθέντος. πάνυ δ᾿ ἀσαφῶς ἐν τούτοις δοκεῖ μοι εἰρηκέναι ὅπερ ἐβούλετο. εἰκὸς δὲ καὶ τὴν κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἀσάφειαν ἐπιτετηδευκέναι αὐτὸν, ἐπείπερ ἑώρα ἰσχυρὸν τὸν λόγον τὸν κατασκευάζοντα ἀπὸ τοιωνδὶ προγόνων εἶναι τὸ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος· πάλιν τ᾿ αὖ ἐβουλήθη μὴ δοκεῖν ἀγνοεῖν πρᾶγμα περὶ Ἰουδαίων καὶ τοῦ γένους αὐτῶν οὐκ εὐκαταφρόνητον. σαφὲς δὴ ὅτι καὶ γενεαλογοῦνται Ἰουδαῖοι ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πατέρων τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τοῦ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τοῦ Ἰακώβ· ὧν τοσοῦτον δύναται τὰ ὀνόματα συναπτόμενα τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ προσηγορίᾳ, ὡς οὐ μόνον τοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἔθνους χρῆσθαι ἐν ταῖς πρὸς θεὸν εὐχαῖς καὶ ἐν τῷ κατεπᾴδειν δαίμονας τῷ ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακὼβ ἀλλὰ γὰρ σχεδὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς τὰ τῶν ἐπῳδῶν καὶ μαγειῶν πραγματευομένους. εὑρίσκεται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς μαγικοῖς συγγράμμασι πολλαχοῦ ἡ τοιαύτη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπίκλησις καὶ παράληψις τοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ ὀνόματος ὡς οἰκείου τοῖς ἀνδράσι τούτοις εἰς τὰ κατὰ τῶν δαιμόνων. ταῦτ᾿ οὖν δοκεῖ μοι, ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων καὶ Χριστιανῶν προσαγόμενα εἰς ἀπόδειξιν τοῦ ἱερούς τινας ἄνδρας γεγονέναι τὸν Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ τὸν Ἰακὼβ, τοὺς πατέρας τοῦ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνους. μὴ πάντῃ μὲν ἠγνοηκέναι ὁ Κέλσος οὐ μὴν σαφῶς ἐκτεθεῖσθαι, ἐπεὶ μὴ ἐδύνατο ἀπαντῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λόγον.
pass_a_gloss: Next after these, Celsus, running over (ἐπιτρέχω) the things from the first book of Moses, which is entitled (ἐπιγράφω) Genesis, says that they then (ἄρα) attempted (ἐπιχειρέω) to trace their genealogy (γενεαλογέω) from a first sowing (σπορά) of sorcerers (γόητες) and deceivers (πλάνοι), calling to witness (ἐπιμαρτύρομαι) faint (ἀμυδρός) and ambiguous (ἀμφίβολος) utterances (φωναί) hidden (κρύφιος) somewhere in darkness (σκότος), and misinterpreting (παρεξηγέομαι) [them] to the unlearned (ἀμαθεῖς) and senseless (ἀνόητοι), and this, in the long time before, such a thing never even having been disputed/claimed (ἀμφισβητέω). Very unclearly (ἀσαφῶς) he seems to me to have said in these what he wished. It is likely (εἰκός) that he also contrived (ἐπιτηδεύω, pf.) the unclarity (ἀσάφεια) in the passage (τόπος), since he saw the argument (λόγος) establishing (κατασκευάζω) that the nation of the Jews is from such-and-such (τοιωνδί) ancestors (πρόγονοι) to be strong (ἰσχυρός); and again on the other hand he wished not to seem ignorant (ἀγνοέω) of a matter about the Jews and their race (γένος) not easily despised (εὐκαταφρόνητος). Clear (σαφές) indeed that the Jews trace their genealogy from the three fathers (πατέρες), Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; whose names, joined (συνάπτω) to the appellation (προσηγορία) of God, have such power (δύναμαι) that not only those of the nation use in prayers (εὐχαί) to God and in charming (κατεπᾴδω) demons the [formula] 'the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob', but also nearly all those practising (πραγματεύομαι) the [arts] of incantations (ἐπῳδαί) and magic (μαγεῖαι). For in magical (μαγικός) writings (συγγράμματα) such invocation (ἐπίκλησις) of God is found in many places, and taking up (παράληψις) of the name of God as belonging (οἰκεῖος) to these men, for the [operations] against the demons. These things then, brought forward (προσάγω) by Jews and Christians for proof (ἀπόδειξις) that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the fathers of the nation of the Jews, were holy (ἱεροί) men, Celsus seems to me not to have been entirely ignorant of, yet not to have set out (ἐκτίθημι) clearly, since he could not meet (ἀπαντάω) the argument.
pass_b_english: Next after this, Celsus, running over the contents of the first book of Moses, which is entitled Genesis, says that “they set about tracing their descent back to a first stock of sorcerers and deceivers, calling to witness faint and ambiguous sayings hidden away somewhere in darkness, and misinterpreting them to the ignorant and foolish; and this though, in all the long time before, no one had ever so much as laid claim to such a thing.” In these words he seems to me to have stated what he meant very obscurely. And it is likely that he contrived the obscurity of this passage on purpose, since he saw that the argument which establishes that the Jewish nation comes from these particular ancestors is strong; and yet, on the other hand, he did not want to seem ignorant of a matter concerning the Jews and their race that is not to be lightly dismissed.

It is clear, then, that the Jews trace their descent from the three fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Their names, joined to the title of God, have such power that the formula “the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob” (Exodus 3:6) is used not only by those of that nation in their prayers to God and in charming away demons, but also by nearly all who busy themselves with spells and magic. For in magical writings this kind of invocation of God is found in many places, as is the use of the name of God as proper to these men, in dealings against the demons. These facts, then, which Jews and Christians bring forward as proof that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the fathers of the Jewish nation, were holy men, Celsus seems to me not to have been wholly ignorant of, and yet not to have set out clearly, since he could not answer the argument.

choices.choice: 'tracing their descent from the first offspring of sorcerers' to 'back to a first stock of sorcerers': πρώτης σπορᾶς γοήτων is the original seed, and the sorcerers are the forebears themselves (Origen's reply turns on Abraham, Isaac and Jacob); 'offspring' wrongly suggested descendants of sorcerers; translator note updated
'as belonging closely to these men' to 'as proper to these men' (οἰκείου; 'closely' was added)

choices.term: θεὸς Αβρααμ καὶ θεὸς Ισαακ καὶ θεὸς Ιακωβ
choices.choice: Checked Exodus 3:6 LXX (θεὸς Αβρααμ καὶ θεὸς Ισαακ καὶ θεὸς Ιακωβ); matches the formula
Speaker check: Celsus's charge (φησὶν ὡς ἄρα ...) is in quotation marks; the rest is Origen

Celsus's charge is reported in indirect speech (φησὶν ὡς ἄρα ...) and is put in double quotation marks as his words. 'a first stock' renders πρώτης σπορᾶς ('first sowing', i.e. original seed; the sorcerers are the forebears themselves, whose names Origen goes on to show are used in magic). The last clause of Celsus's charge, τοῦ τοιοῦδε μηδ᾿ ἀμφισβητηθέντος, is doubtful in sense: ἀμφισβητέω can mean 'dispute' or 'lay claim to'; taken here as 'no one had ever so much as laid claim to such a thing' (no one had claimed such descent before). 'these particular ancestors' renders τοιωνδὶ προγόνων. The formula 'the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob' matches Exodus 3:6 LXX (also Exodus 3:15-16; quoted in Matthew 22:32); Exodus 3:6 is cited. 'charming away demons' renders κατεπᾴδειν δαίμονας (subduing demons by incantation, i.e. exorcism); Origen returns to this use of the patriarchs' names in 4.34. The staged text punctuates with full stops before ἥτις and before μὴ πάντῃ; both are read as part of the same sentence. Holy men renders ἱερούς (sacred, holy).
